summary: Rivière-du-Loup Airport (YRI) is a regional airport serving the Bas-Saint-Laurent region of Quebec, located near the south shore of the St. Lawrence River. It primarily supports general aviation, air ambulance services, and occasional regional flights, serving as an important access point for this scenic area of eastern Quebec.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly from Rivière-du-Loup Airport?
A: The airport mainly serves general aviation and charter flights, with no scheduled commercial passenger service currently operating on a regular basis.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Rivière-du-Loup?
A: The airport is located just a few kilometers northeast of the city center, making it a quick drive from downtown.

Q: Are there customs and immigration services available?
A: The airport has limited Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) clearance capabilities, typically requiring advance arrangement for international flights.

Q: Can I land a private aircraft at YRI?
A: Yes, the airport welcomes private general aviation aircraft, and pilots should check current NOTAMs and contact the airport for fuel and service availability.
transport_tips: Taxis and rental cars are the most common ground transport options, though services are limited due to the airport's small size. Pre-arranging a rental car is strongly recommended as on-site options are scarce. The drive to downtown Rivière-du-Loup takes only about 10 minutes via Route 132.
local_tip: If you're flying in, time your visit around sunset to catch spectacular views of the St. Lawrence River and the Charlevoix mountains across the water—a photographer's dream from this part of Quebec.
